title: Equivariant Diffusion Policy
layout_note: a 2x2 commuting square: the top row maps an observation to its gradient field, the bottom row maps the 90-degree-rotated observation to its field, and two downward 'Rot 90' arrows link the rows
grouping: Four square black-framed panels in a 2x2 grid with no outer container: left column = toy observations (o, g o), right column = the same scenes with a gradient field ('Gradient Field'). Two orange-outlined callout boxes with formulas sit in the gutter between the rows, centred under/over the right column.
shapes_depth: Flat 2-D toy scene: a black gripper glyph (a T-shaped bracket), a blue L-shaped obstacle and a green square goal; on the right the gripper is repeated in a black-to-light-grey sequence of poses along a thin trajectory line over a field of small black arrows. Hollow white block arrows connect panels; curved rotation glyphs label the vertical arrows. Tiny orange squares mark one field location in each right panel.
proposed_highlight: The defining property is the geometry itself: the bottom row is the top row rotated 90 degrees, and orange callout boxes with matching tiny orange squares pick out one field vector before and after rotation.
lesson: Show an equivariance property as a commuting square on a tiny toy instance: the operation along the rows, the symmetry transform down the columns, and one matching-tint marker tying the same sampled vector in both transformed outputs.
notes: Method short name EquiDiff (the paper's abbreviation for Equivariant Diffusion Policy). Venue and year from the PDF first-page footer (8th Conference on Robot Learning, CoRL 2024). The architecture figure (Figure 3) was judged weaker (long blue wires routed round the panel edge to the U-Net, a long return loop on the left) and `refs crop` could not find its wrapped caption; Figure 2 is carded as the figure that draws the method's defining property. Figure 2 is one embedded raster recorded by refs crop, so measured.photo_share is null and the palette is taken from the whole raster.

arrangement.units: four black-framed square panels in a 2x2 grid; the two rows are the same scene before and after a 90-degree rotation; formula callouts in orange-outlined boxes sit between the rows
arrangement.inputs_as: a toy 2-D scene (gripper glyph, blue obstacle, green goal) labelled o and g o
arrangement.shared: the same denoising map is the unlabeled horizontal arrow in both rows

taxonomy.task: visuomotor policy learning with an SO(2)-equivariant denoising function
taxonomy.note: architecture other: the figure draws no network, only the equivariance of the denoising function as a commuting square on a toy scene and its gradient field

insights.structure: A 2x2 grid where rows are the operation (observation to gradient field) and columns are the symmetry (rotate 90 degrees), so equivariance reads as a square that commutes.
insights.data: The observation is a minimal toy scene (gripper bracket, blue obstacle, green goal) and the output is the same scene with a full arrow field and a grey-graded sequence of gripper poses along the denoised trajectory.
insights.emphasis: Orange callout boxes between the rows and tiny orange squares in the corners of both field panels single out one vector and show it rotating with the scene.
insights.flow: Read the top row left to right, then down the 'Rot 90' arrows; all connections are short, straight hollow block arrows between adjacent panels.
insights.avoid: The relation is stated twice, once by the rotated panels and again by typeset formulas inside the orange callout boxes, and the horizontal map arrows carry no label.

core.what: the denoising map drawn on a small toy scene as a 2x2 commuting square: operation along rows, 90-degree rotation down columns

relations.form: the denoising function is shown as an arrow field and a sequence of gripper poses drawn directly over a toy 2-D scene with obstacle and goal
the bottom row repeats the top row's two panels with the scene rotated 90 degrees, linked by downward 'Rot 90' block arrows
a tiny orange square in the corner of each field panel is tied by matching orange outline to a callout box quoting that one vector

channels.colour: blue = obstacle, green = goal, black-to-grey = successive gripper poses along the trajectory (grey level = step), orange = the highlighted sample and its callout
channels.shape: bracket glyph = gripper, L-shape = obstacle, square = goal, small arrows = field vectors; hollow block arrows = maps between panels
channels.line: hollow block arrows for maps between panels; thin black line for the trajectory; no dashed lines
channels.frame: black square frame = one scene; orange outline = the highlighted sample and its formula

quality.strengths: The method's defining property is visible as geometry without reading a label (the bottom row is the top row rotated); the operation is drawn on a small instance of the structure, as derive.md asks; each colour has one meaning; all connections are short straight block arrows between adjacent panels; orange tint ties the corner marker to its callout.
quality.weaknesses: The orange callouts typeset formulas (epsilon(o, eps^k, k) = arrow) in boxes rather than drawing the terms; the grey grading of the gripper poses is not keyed; the horizontal map arrows are unlabeled, so the denoising function is named only inside the callouts; the arrow fields are dense enough to compete with the trajectory.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
